_meta.description: Niche profile for Hindi health education channel. Every pipeline stage reads from this file. Do not hardcode any of these values inside stage scripts.

editorial.target_audience_description: Hindi-speaking middle-aged and older adults (35-65) managing or preventing chronic conditions like diabetes, hypertension, and heart disease. They speak everyday conversational Hindi mixed with common English words — they say 'diabetes' not 'madhumeh', 'BP' not 'raktachaap'. They do NOT understand Sanskritized/formal Hindi medical terminology. High motivation to act on credible health information.
editorial.tone_description: Like a knowledgeable friend who happens to have a medical background. Never condescending, never alarmist. Speaks directly — 'aapko' not 'logon ko'. Makes the listener feel informed and capable, not scared.
terminology_rules: ALWAYS use the term that a modern Hindi speaker actually says out loud. If the English/borrowed term is what people say, use that — written in Roman script within the Devanagari sentence. Examples: write 'diabetes' not 'madhumeh', 'blood pressure' not 'raktachaap', 'heart attack' not 'hriday aaghat', 'protein' not 'protheen', 'calcium' not 'kailshiyam', 'exercise' not 'vyayam', 'stress' not 'tanav' (unless the Hindi word is equally common in speech).
Pure Sanskritized Hindi medical terms (madhumeh, raktachaap, hriday, etc.) are NOT understood by modern audiences and must NOT be used.
If a technical term is unfamiliar in any form, briefly explain it in plain Hindi on first use — but still use the common spoken form, not a Sanskrit equivalent.
Never use jargon without explanation. Every term introduced must have context from the surrounding sentence.
Avoid passive constructions — prefer active, direct phrasing.

For statistics, always convert to simple percentages or plain fractions that a layperson understands — '22% कम risk' or '3 गुना ज़्यादा'. Never say 'RR', 'OR', 'HR', 'SMD', 'confidence interval', or 'p-value' in the spoken script. Pick at most 2-3 numbers total.

segment_structure.name: hook
segment_structure.purpose: Open with the core surprising finding as a direct statement or rhetorical question that immediately makes the viewer feel this matters to their life. Must reference the study. No generic openers like 'Aaj hum baat karenge'. Make it personal — why should THIS person watching care RIGHT NOW.
example_openings: Ek naye shodh mein paaya gaya ki...
Kya aap jaante hain ki sirf [X] din mein...
[N] hazaar logon par kiye gaye adhyayan ne sabit kiya ki...

segment_structure.name: context
segment_structure.purpose: Who conducted the study, how many people, what type of study, and crucially — WHY this research was done and what problem it was trying to solve. Explain what this condition or topic actually does to a person's daily life in simple terms before presenting the science. Build credibility through the journal and sample size.

segment_structure.name: finding
segment_structure.purpose: The core result with exact numbers, AND a full plain-language explanation of what it means for a normal person. CRITICAL: Name each specific intervention by its exact name (e.g. 'Mediterranean diet', 'aerobic exercise', '7-8 ghante ki neend', 'omega-3') — never just say 'lifestyle changes' or 'healthy habits' without specifying what those are. Cover: (1) what the study found with the 1-2 most striking percentages (never raw RR/OR/SMD notation) and named interventions, (2) what this means in practical terms — how it could improve, worsen, or change someone's daily life, energy, health, or longevity, (3) the biological or behavioural mechanism in simple words (why does this happen?), (4) who benefits most and who may not. This is the heart of the video — do not rush it. Use relatable analogies.

segment_structure.name: caveat
segment_structure.purpose: What the study does NOT prove. Who this may not apply to. Key limitations. Frame it as 'here is what we still don't know' rather than undermining the finding. Every video must have this. Be honest but constructive.

segment_structure.name: actionable_takeaway
segment_structure.purpose: One or two concrete, safe actions the viewer can take today based on the evidence. Make it specific and doable — not 'eat healthy' but 'replace your afternoon snack with X'. Frame as a suggestion. Never recommend stopping medications or substituting professional advice.

segment_structure.name: cta
segment_structure.purpose: Subscribe + comment CTA. Keep it natural, not robotic. One of the pre-approved CTA variants below.
cta_variants: Agar yeh jaankari useful lagi, toh channel ko subscribe karein aur comment mein batayein ki aap kis topic par aur jaanna chahte hain.
Is video ko apne kisi khaas insaan ke saath share karein jise yeh jaankari kaam aa sakti hai.
Neeche comment mein apna sawaal likhein — hum agli video mein jawab dene ki koshish karenge.

script.script_language_instruction: The entire voiceover script (hindi_script and every hindi_text field) MUST be written in Devanagari script for all Hindi words. All Hindi words must be in Devanagari (e.g. आपको, क्या — NOT 'aapko', 'kya'). HOWEVER: English words that modern Hindi speakers actually say out loud MUST remain in Roman script — this includes both medical terms (diabetes, blood pressure, heart attack, protein, calcium, exercise, stress, BMI, cholesterol, insulin) AND common everyday English (study, research, diet, lifestyle, healthy, weight, ok, actually, basically, fat, muscle, gut, immune, gut bacteria, inflammation). Do NOT replace these with Sanskrit/Hindi equivalents — never 'madhumeh', 'raktachaap', 'adhyayan', 'vyayam'. The test is: would a 45-year-old in Delhi say this word in normal conversation? If they'd say it in English, keep it in Roman. VOCABULARY must be colloquial — use 'log' not 'vyakti/vayask', 'doctor se baat karo' not 'paraamarsh lein', 'pata chala' not 'prakaash mein aaya'. EXAMPLE — ❌ Formal: 'ek adhyayan mein 96 vayaskon ko shaamil kiya gaya aur paraamarsh ke liye kaha gaya' ✅ Modern: 'ek study mein 96 logon ko shaamil kiya gaya aur doctor se milne ko kaha gaya'.
absolute_prohibitions: Never use causal language ('causes', 'cures', 'prevents') for observational studies
Never recommend stopping or modifying prescribed medications
Never make absolute health claims without qualifying with 'shodh ke anusaar' or 'adhyayan mein paaya gaya'
Never reference a study without mentioning sample size somewhere in the script
Never open with 'Namaste doston, aaj ki video mein' or similar generic openers
Never end with 'Toh yeh thi aaj ki jaankari' or similar filler closings

Never transliterate Hindi words into Roman script — Hindi words must always be Devanagari (never write 'aapko', always write 'आपको'). English words that modern Hindi speakers actually say out loud must stay in Roman script — this includes both medical terms AND common everyday English like 'study', 'diet', 'ok', 'basically'.

Never use vague umbrella terms like 'lifestyle changes', 'healthy habits', or 'better choices' without immediately naming the specific behaviours — e.g. write 'Mediterranean diet, aerobic exercise, 7-8 ghante ki neend' not just 'lifestyle mein badlaav'. Every specific_intervention extracted from the study must be named individually in the script.

visuals.broll_style_description: Real people doing real things. Prefer footage of South Asian or racially ambiguous individuals aged 35-65. Avoid obviously Western stock footage (blonde people in gyms, US hospital interiors). Prefer natural lighting, home or outdoor settings.

broll_mood_map.context: neutral, clinical but approachable — lab, doctor-patient, reading
broll_mood_map.finding: direct illustration of the topic — food, exercise, sleep, body
broll_mood_map.caveat: thoughtful, calm — person thinking, doctor consulting
broll_mood_map.actionable_takeaway: positive, active — person doing the recommended action
broll_mood_map.cta: warm, community — group of people, family

avoid_in_broll: Syringes or blood unless directly relevant
Overweight people used to illustrate disease (avoid stigmatizing imagery)
Hospital ICU or emergency settings unless directly relevant
Stock photos of people faking illness

style_variants.description: Bold statistic or percentage as the dominant text element, clean background, one supporting icon or minimal illustration. High contrast.
A real-looking person (South Asian, middle-aged) in a relatable health context. Warm tones. Facial expression is curious or relieved, not alarmed.
A clean metaphorical visual representing the study topic. E.g. a gut represented as a garden, a brain as a glowing network. Minimal text overlay.

text_overlay_rules: Must be readable at 120x68px (YouTube mobile thumbnail size)
No red circles or arrows — overused and flagged by YouTube quality systems
Hindi text preferred on thumbnail for audience signal

background_music.notes: Manually curate 5-8 royalty-free tracks from Pixabay Music. Store in /assets/music/. Do not automate music selection — pick once, rotate across videos.

medical_disclaimer.text_hindi: यह वीडियो केवल शैक्षिक उद्देश्यों के लिए है। किसी भी स्वास्थ्य संबंधी निर्णय के लिए अपने चिकित्सक से परामर्श लें।
medical_disclaimer.text_english: This video is for educational purposes only. Consult your doctor before making any health decisions.

ai_disclosure.description_text: This video was created with AI assistance. All health claims are sourced from peer-reviewed research cited in the description.

compliance.industry_funding_disclosure: Agar yeh adhyayan kisi company dwara funded tha, toh script mein yeh zaroor mention karein.
compliance.observational_study_language_rule: If study_type is observational or cross-sectional, script must use 'sambandh paaya gaya' (association found) not 'sabit hua ki' (proven that)

youtube_upload.tags_instruction: Generate 25-35 tags total covering three scripts: (1) English tags for the topic and study keywords, (2) Hinglish tags (Hindi words in Roman script, e.g. 'diabetes ke upay', 'sugar control kaise kare'), (3) Devanagari tags (same keywords in Hindi script, e.g. 'मधुमेह उपाय', 'शुगर कंट्रोल'). YouTube allows up to 500 characters total — keep each tag short. The default tags are already included; generate additional topic-specific tags only.
